messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Testing Distributions
parts:
Is there a way to run test-distributions so that when one distribution
test fails, the rest keep running?


Peter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Testing Distributions
parts: Add -k to the make test-distributions call

On Saturday, June 22, 2013 12:02:37 AM UTC-4, Peter Li wrote:
Is there a way to run test-distributions so that when one distribution
test fails, the rest keep running?


Peter

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Testing Distributions
parts:
The issue isn't the -k flag. When you add the parallelization flag with it being greater or equal to 3, make doesn't detect failures properly. The solution is to run it without the -j flag or set it to 2. The other solution is to run the target again after running it once without the -j flag. That will pick up the failure and it won't spend the time compiling. 

I believe the way the target is set up, it will compile everything first, so it won't detect failures until runtime if it compiles. You could run a single test if you know what distribution you are testing. 



Daniel
On Jun 21, 2013, at 10:59 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

Add -k to the make test-distributions call

On Saturday, June 22, 2013 12:02:37 AM UTC-4, Peter Li wrote:
Is there a way to run test-distributions so that when one distribution
test fails, the rest keep running?


Peter

Then where does the problem originate? This erroneous patch

diff --git a/src/test/agrad/agrad_test.cpp b/src/test/agrad/agrad_test.cpp
index dc15f91..772ec2a 100644
--- a/src/test/agrad/agrad_test.cpp
+++ b/src/test/agrad/agrad_test.cpp
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 #include <gtest/gtest.h>
 #include <stan/agrad/agrad.hpp>
-#include <test/agrad/util.hpp>
+#include <test/agrad/utils.hpp>

 TEST(AgradRev, multiple_grads) {
   for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {

yields the expected behavior

make clean-all > /dev/null && make CC=clang++ -j9 test-unit > /tmp/clang++.log && echo "success"
...
src/test/agrad/agrad_test.cpp:3:10: fatal error: 'test/agrad/utils.hpp' file not found
#include <test/agrad/utils.hpp>
         ^
1 error generated.
make: *** [test/agrad/agrad.o] Error 1
make: *** Waiting for unfinished jobs....

Ben
